title: AI Governance SME & Advisor
description:
**Role Description**
AI Governance SME & Advisor — Role Description Programme: AI Security & Governance Programme Role overview We are seeking an experienced AI Governance SME to help establish, operationalise and embed our Client's enterprise AI governance framework as part of their AI Security & Governance Programme. You will advise senior stakeholders on how to govern AI responsibly and securely at enterprise scale, and on the establishment of frameworks, registers, processes and controls that make governance real. You will bring hands-on experience of AI governance frameworks, AI boards, registers and management processes: their use within large enterprises, and will be comfortable operationalising these through a dedicated AI Governance platform that acts as the client's system of record, risk management and control for AI. Key responsibilities AI governance framework and operating model (establishment and advisory)
  
  

* Design and establish the enterprise AI governance framework and target operating model, aligned to recognised standards and regulation (eg. ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act and the OECD AI Principles).
* Liaise with senior stakeholders to establish the AI Governance Board / AI Council — defining its mandate, membership, decision rights, terms of reference, escalation routes, meeting cadence and reporting lines — and integrate it with existing data, privacy, security, risk and procurement forums
* Liaise with senior stakeholder to define the AI governance operating model, including roles, responsibilities and a clear RACI across all stakeholder groups
* Design and stand up the AI use-case lifecycle: intake, triage, risk assessment, review, approval, ongoing monitoring and decommissioning
* Ensure AI policies, standards, acceptable-use guidance and Responsible AI principles (fairness, transparency, accountability, explainability and human oversight) are embedded into governance gates
* Act as trusted advisor and SME to leadership on AI governance, maturity uplift, and regulatory developments AI register, inventory and ownership
* Establish the AI Register as a single source of truth — including AI asset classification, risk tiering, risk mitigations and clear ownership and accountability AI Governance platform enablement
* Lead requirements definition, configuration and operationalisation of the client's AI Governance platform, covering workflows, registers, risk assessments, control libraries, evidence capture and reporting
* Map governance processes to platform workflows so that inventory, risk assessment, approvals and assurance are managed and evidenced through the platform AI risk management
* Support the development of templates for the AI risk taxonomy, risk-tiering methodology, controls mapping, exception and waiver framework and associated governance processes AI security controls and assessment (delivery)
* Support delivery of the programme, ensuring roadmap activities are progressed and tracked across all workstreams
* Develop and operationalise AI security controls, standards and procedures aligned to the AI framework
* Develop plans and processes for technical assessments of AI platforms, AI-enabled applications, AI agents, MCP integrations and embedded vendor AI capabilities
* Liaise with expert teams to define the security requirements for AI agents, including identity, privilege management, logging, monitoring, recertification and approval processes
* Create security guidance for AI development, secure prompt engineering, model consumption and AI-assisted development (“vibe coding”) practices Monitoring, shadow AI and incident response
* Establish AI security monitoring requirements and work with the Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) to develop detections, use cases, dashboards and reporting
* Support shadow AI discovery through analysis of Microsoft, AWS, SAP and other telemetry sources, helping identify unsanctioned AI usage and associated risks Reporting and assurance
* Produce management reporting, implementation metrics, control-effectiveness measures and quarterly assurance outputs for leadership review
* [Real-time monitoring for all registered AI assets in production?] Required skills and experience
* Demonstrable knowledge of the establishment of enterprise AI governance frameworks, operating models and AI governance boards
* Hands-on knowledge of the definition of AI registers and inventories, ownership models and AI management processes
* Sound understanding of AI regulation and standards, including the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF, together with data-protection considerations (UK GDPR)
* AI security knowledge, ideally including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS, and experience of AI threat modelling
* Excellent stakeholder management, advisory and communication skills, with the credibility to influence at senior and executive level Desirable qualifications
* ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor
* IAPP AIGP (Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional)
* Relevant cloud certifications

**Skills**
AI Governance, AI Register Management, Threat Modeling, Risk Management, Cloud Security, Compliance Management, AI Security

title: Manager, Credit Risk Governance
description:
****Key Responsibilities****
**Operational Risk Framework for Credit Risk and Stressed Asset Risk (SAR)**

* Own and oversee the monthly Operational Risk assessment processes, maintain and update the Credit Risk Register and Risk and Control Self-Assessment for both Credit Risk and SAR.
* Facilitate the completion of Control Tests (KCIs/CSTs) and other governance and control checks. Assist to identify and assess key operational risk areas and control gaps.
* Engage in periodic trigger reviews, Inherent and Residual Risk Assessments, Risk register reviews, risk acceptances, control documents and other regular assessments and ensure that outcomes are appropriately reflected in the relevant governance and reporting systems.
* Investigate exceptions, maintain supporting evidence, track remediation, and escalate material or overdue matters where required.
* Address data-quality issues and support the ongoing maintenance and accuracy of governance records.

**Prudential Compliance Framework**

* Maintain and update the PCF register for the applicable regulatory requirements (i.e. CRR, PRA Rulebook, PRA Supervisory Statements, and EBA Technical Standards) where Credit Risk RFO is the chapter owner
* Coordinate attestation / confirmation of the articles assigned to the various line owners as part of the quarterly and annual attestation exercise. The attestation/confirmation should be supported by a ‘deep dive’ review, which would entail obtaining documentary evidence for a sample of requirements to confirm that controls and control assurance methods documented in the compliance registers are working effectively;
* Identify appropriate line owner(s) for each changed regulation and ensure timely escalation of regulatory changes to the relevant stakeholders;
* Facilitate annual attestation and quarterly confirmation by CRO CIB Risk / delegate as Chapter Owner by providing them the result of the acceptance by line owners, any material regulatory changes, and gaps/breaches (if any), for onward submission to Group Compliance;
* Ensure that control and assurance methods documented by line owners provide a sufficiently robust control framework to enable effective ongoing compliance, including exception monitoring / reporting;
* Prepare Prudential Regulatory Compliance (Credit Risk) report semi-annually covering the yearly attestation, issues encountered during the exercise and plan/s to resolve with clear timelines for submission to Credit Risk Committee;
* Co-ordinate/support the management of audits relevant to Prudential Compliance;

**ICAAP and Regulatory Capital**

* Coordinate the annual Credit Risk ICAAP Pillar 2A assessment process.
* Review proposed Credit Risk Pillar 2A capital add-ons and supporting RWA and capital narratives and maintain supporting methodology, analysis, and governance documentation.
* Assess existing and emerging credit risks to determine whether additional Pillar 2A capital may be required.
* Prepare, reconcile, and validate supporting data and perform relevant KCI and CST checks.
* Coordinate stakeholder review and sign-off of Group and Solo ICAAP submissions.
* Prepare materials for Expert Panel reviews, including the methodology review and final capital assessment.

**Credit NFRC Governance and Secretariat**

* Support the effective operation of the Credit Non-Financial Risk Committee.
* Coordinate agenda setting, meeting timelines, paper submission, pack consolidation, quorum, minutes, and follow-up actions.
* Prepare the committee’s summary and escalation paper.
* Coordinate the annual review of the committee Terms of Reference and the periodic committee effectiveness assessment.
* Review and consolidate relevant Credit NFRC papers and management information, including EA and covenant reporting, SAR KCI reporting, Credit KCI reporting, quarterly KCI and CST exceptions, and policy exceptions.

****Other Responsibilities****

* Coordinate the annual and periodic review of intragroup outsourcing arrangements.
* Maintain SAR delegated authority letters and coordinate updates to relevant systems when there are changes.
* Support Senior Credit Secretariat requests on SCS Sole/Dual approval process when required
* Support the team with various reports such as Headcount reporting, Conduct dashboard etc.
* Responsible to update the Conduct outcomes and Conflict of Interest register in discussion with Group Compliance
* Perform other credit governance activities and other projects, as assigned

**Processes**

* Support Credit RFO / Credit PU owner in supervising the Credit Processes.
* Ensure compliance with applicable internal policies, and external laws and regulations, related to Credit Risk.
* Continuously improve the operational efficiency and effectiveness of the risk management processes.

**People & Talent**

* Lead through example and demonstrate the appropriate culture and values within the function and across the wider organisation.

**Risk Management**

* Maintain a good understanding of the requirements of key external stakeholders in respect of risk management and ensure these are well understood internally and reflected in internal procedures.
* Obtain assurance regarding the effectiveness of the policy controls and compliance with applicable laws & regulations.
* Maintain an open and cooperative relationship in dealings with internal and external stakeholders

**Governance**

* Responsible for ensuring effective Risk Governance

**Regulatory & Business Conduct**

* Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
* Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
* Support the Credit policy team to achieve the outcomes set out in the Bank’s Conduct Principles
* Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

**Key stakeholders**

* Credit Approvers
* Relationship Managers / COO Office
* Enterprise Risk Management
* SAG/ SAR
* CCRO / Country Credit Governance teams
* Treasury
* CIC Modelling
* Credit Risk Control (Middle Office)
* Credit Risk Infrastructure
* Traded Risk Management
* Operational Risk
* Group Internal Audit
* Legal
* Compliance

****Other Responsibilities****

* Embed Here for good and Group’s brand and values in CIB Risk team; Perform other responsibilities assigned under Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures

****Skills And Experience****

* Credit Risk Governance
* Operational Risk Controls
* Stakeholder Management
* Strong analytical, communication and interpersonal skills.
* Regulations impacting Credit Risk

****Qualifications****

* Strong knowledge of credit risk governance
* Experience in governance and control testing, risk registers, RCSA, KCI/CST monitoring, and issue remediation.
* Has good understanding of operating risk identification process and implementing process controls. Experience in working / implementing such methodology in process operations would be preferable.
* Understanding of Basel requirements, regulatory capital, ICAAP, and Pillar 2A and their impact on credit policy, processes, controls, and systems.
* Experience supporting senior governance committees and preparing executive-level papers, management information, and presentations.
* Strong analytical skills, including the ability to review capital and RWA information, reconcile data, challenge assumptions, and identify material issues.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex regulatory and risk matters into clear governance documentation.
* Ability to coordinate multiple ad hoc deliverables.
* Strong stakeholder-management skills and confidence engaging senior stakeholders across multiple functions and jurisdictions.
* High attention to detail, sound judgement, and the ability to work independently while maintaining effective governance and control discipline.

****About Standard Chartered****
We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.
  
  
Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.
  
  
**Together We:**

* Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
* Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

****What We Offer****
**In line with our Fair Pay Charter,**
we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.
  
  

* Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
* Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.

* A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.

title: FinCrime - Compliance - Consulting Lead - Senior Manager
description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.
  
  
**Senior Manager, Financial Crime Compliance Consulting Lead, EY GDS Consulting**
Global Delivery Services is one of EY's greatest global assets – a network of service delivery centers that provide high-quality services at a competitive cost for all EY’s client serving and enablement teams. Every day, we combine our subject matter expertise with our technology and automation skills to develop new solutions that deliver greater value for EY. If you have a passion for enabling world class actuarial services globally to solve the most complex challenges in the financial services industry, come join our dynamic GDS team!
  
  
**The opportunity**
We are seeking an accomplished Financial Crime Compliance consulting professional with strong domain expertise in AML, KYC, regulatory compliance and financial crime risk management.
  
  
The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of independently leading complex consulting engagements, advising senior leadership and C-suite stakeholders, and delivering regulatory and AML framework assessments for financial services clients.
  
  
This role requires deep regulatory knowledge, strategic advisory capabilities and strong consulting acumen, with the ability to translate complex compliance challenges into practical, risk-based and commercially sustainable solutions.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities**
**Financial Crime Advisory and Consulting**

* Independently lead end-to-end Financial Crime Compliance consulting engagements across banking, financial services, FinTech and payments clients.
* Conduct comprehensive assessments of AML/KYC frameworks, regulatory compliance programs, governance structures and financial crime control environments.
* Advise clients on AML/CFT regulatory obligations, industry best practices and evolving financial crime risks.
* Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of financial crime controls, identify gaps and recommend sustainable remediation strategies.
* Lead regulatory gap assessments, compliance maturity assessments, target operating model reviews and financial crime transformation initiatives.

**Regulatory Framework and Risk Assessments**

* Assess client compliance frameworks against applicable regulatory requirements and international standards, including FATF recommendations and relevant jurisdiction-specific AML/CFT regulations.
* Lead enterprise-wide financial crime risk assessments, customer risk assessment framework reviews and risk-based due diligence evaluations.
* Review policies, procedures, governance models, monitoring mechanisms and escalation frameworks.
* Develop regulatory remediation roadmaps, control enhancement recommendations and risk mitigation strategies.
* Support regulatory examination preparedness, independent compliance reviews and audit remediation programs.

**C Suite Advisory and Stakeholder Management**

* Independently manage strategic discussions with C-suite executives, Chief Compliance Officers, MLROs, Chief Risk Officers and senior business leaders.
* Present regulatory assessment findings, compliance risks, strategic recommendations and transformation roadmaps to executive leadership.
* Facilitate senior stakeholder workshops, challenge existing control frameworks constructively and influence risk-based decision-making.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to clients on complex financial crime compliance matters.
* Build and maintain strong executive relationships while managing stakeholder expectations throughout consulting engagements.

**Consulting Engagement Leadership**

* Own consulting assignments from initial scoping and diagnostic assessment through solution design, delivery and executive presentation.
* Lead client workshops, stakeholder interviews, regulatory gap analyses and compliance framework evaluations.
* Develop high-quality consulting deliverables, including assessment reports, maturity models, executive dashboards, regulatory gap analyses and strategic recommendations.
* Manage project governance, delivery milestones, risks, dependencies and stakeholder communications.
* Guide cross-functional consulting teams and ensure timely delivery of high-quality advisory outcomes.

**Business Development and Consulting Capability Building**

* Contribute to client proposals, RFP responses, solution design and consulting opportunity assessments.
* Identify opportunities to expand Financial Crime Compliance advisory services within existing and prospective client accounts.
* Develop reusable consulting methodologies, assessment frameworks, diagnostic tools and thought leadership content.
* Support capability building, knowledge sharing and mentoring of junior consultants.

**Skills And Attributes For Success**
Skills and attributes for a successful career at EY require a learning mindset and a passion for adding value to GDS, member firms and client organizations. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong technical judgement, delivery ownership, inclusive leadership and the ability to build trusted relationships across locations.
  
  
**To qualify for the role, you must have**

* 8–10 years of relevant professional experience, with substantial exposure to Financial Crime Compliance advisory, regulatory consulting or risk management.
* Prior experience with a Big Four consulting firm is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience independently managing Financial Crime Compliance consulting engagements for financial services clients.
* Proven expertise in regulatory/AML framework assessments, compliance gap analyses, financial crime risk assessments and control effectiveness reviews.
* Strong understanding of AML/CFT regulations, FATF standards, KYC/CDD/EDD requirements, transaction monitoring and financial crime governance.
* Demonstrated ability to engage, influence and present recommendations to C-suite and senior compliance leadership.
* Experience developing executive-level presentations, assessment reports, remediation strategies and regulatory advisory deliverables.
* Strong consulting, analytical, problem-solving, project management and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Professional certifications such as CAMS, ICA, CFE or equivalent Financial Crime Compliance credentials.
* Experience advising multinational banks, payment institutions, FinTech organizations or other regulated financial institutions.
* Exposure to regulatory remediation programs, AML compliance transformation, operating model design and process optimization.
* Familiarity with international regulatory environments, including the US, UK, EU and APAC.
* Experience contributing to consulting practice development, client acquisition or advisory solution design.

**Ideally, you’ll also have**

* Consulting Leadership: Ability to independently structure, manage and deliver complex client engagements.
* Regulatory Expertise: Strong command of AML/CFT regulatory expectations and financial crime control frameworks.
* Executive Presence: Confidence and credibility in engaging C-suite executives and senior compliance stakeholders.
* Strategic Problem Solving: Ability to convert regulatory findings into actionable business recommendations.
* Client Relationship Management: Ability to build trusted advisory relationships and influence decisions.
* Delivery Excellence: Strong ownership of consulting outcomes, quality, timelines and client satisfaction.

**What We Look For**

* Independently lead and deliver complex FinCrime consulting assignments with minimal supervision.
* Establish credibility with C-suite stakeholders and act as a trusted regulatory and compliance advisor.
* Identify material regulatory and control gaps and recommend pragmatic, risk-based remediation solutions.
* Deliver executive-ready assessments and strategic recommendations that strengthen clients’ financial crime compliance frameworks.
* Contribute to the growth and development of the Financial Crime Compliance consulting practice.
* We are looking for a consultant who can independently lead engagements, challenge existing frameworks, influence executive decisions and translate regulatory complexity into measurable compliance improvements.
* The ideal candidate brings the regulatory depth of a FinCrime specialist, the structured problem-solving approach of a management consultant and the executive presence required to advise senior leadership.

**What We Offer**

title: Legal Associate
description:
**WE ARE HIRING!**

**Associate | Chennai**

Applications are invited from advocates interested in joining the litigation practice of
**Mr Ravi Kiran M,**
who presently serves as Standing Counsel for the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB) and its constituent corporations, while continuing his association with M/s. Mothilal & Goda.

**About the Practice**

Mr Ravi Kiran M practises before the Madras High Court and various courts and tribunals in Chennai and across India.

A substantial portion of the practice involves representing the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board and its constituent corporations, including TNPDCL, TNPGCL, TNGECL and TANTRANSCO, in writ litigation, commercial and civil disputes, arbitration proceedings and other matters before the Madras High Court, National Green Tribunal (NGT), National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRT), Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals (DRAT), Arbitral Tribunals, City Civil Courts and other subordinate courts, as well as various Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils across India.

The practice also encompasses private commercial arbitrations, writ litigation, commercial and civil disputes, real estate and property disputes, including proceedings before the Madras High Court, the Tamil Nadu Real Estate Regulatory Authority (TNRERA), the Tamil Nadu Real Estate Appellate Tribunal (TNREAT) and the City Civil Courts, as well as transactional and advisory work relating to commercial and real estate matters.

**Positions Available**

Applications are invited for the following positions:

1. **Associate – 1 to 3 years of experience:**
   Candidates with experience or a demonstrated interest in litigation, legal research and drafting.
2. **Associate – 3 to 4 years of experience:**
   Candidates with demonstrated experience in litigation before the NCLT/NCLAT, in addition to general litigation experience.

*(Candidates with less than one year of experience are also welcome to apply and will be considered for an interview if their applications are found suitable.)*

**Nature of Work**

The positions are primarily litigation-orientated and based in Chennai.

Associates will be involved in legal research, drafting pleadings, preparing matters for hearings, briefing counsel, attending court proceedings and independently handling assignments.

Associates will be given opportunities to appear before courts and tribunals and argue applications and cases, depending on the nature of the proceedings and their experience and preparedness.

The role requires associates to take ownership of their assignments, manage competing responsibilities and work effectively within tight deadlines.

**Qualities We Look For**

We seek candidates who demonstrate a strong work ethic, intellectual curiosity, a willingness to learn and the ability to work collaboratively under pressure. Applicants should take ownership of their assignments and be willing to undertake responsibilities irrespective of their nature or complexity.

**Location, Language and Travel Requirements**

Applicants must be based in Chennai and should possess a reasonable command of reading and writing in Tamil, in addition to proficiency in English.

Given the nature of the practice, associates must be willing to travel outside Chennai for hearings and other professional commitments. Applicants are also expected to have their own vehicles as the role will involve frequent travel between courts, tribunals and other offices within the city.

**Remuneration**

Remuneration will be commensurate with experience and suitability and will be discussed during the interview.

**Application Process**

Interested candidates may send their
**CV along with a covering email**
to
**admin@mothilalgoda.com.**

title: Manager - Transfer Pricing
description:
**Job Summary**

* The Direct and Indirect Tax Change Champion exists to translate tax strategy, legislative developments and operational requirements into controlled, sustainable changes across direct and indirect tax processes. The role enables Tax teams to adopt new policies, processes, data capabilities and technologies while maintaining regulatory compliance, operational continuity and effective internal controls.
* The role is accountable for shaping and delivering tax transformation initiatives, coordinating impact assessments, strengthening process and data controls, and preparing affected stakeholders for implementation. This includes establishing clear transformation governance, managing dependencies and risks, and using process analysis and tax expertise to identify opportunities for automation, standardisation and improved reporting.
* Working across Country and Group Tax teams, Finance, Technology and relevant business functions, the role influences tax process owners and supports subject-matter experts in converting regulatory and business requirements into practical solutions. The role does not own underlying tax legislation, business strategy or technology development. It provides the change leadership, tax context and governance required to implement agreed changes effectively.

**Key Responsibilities**
**Tax Transformation Strategy & Prioritisation**

* Translate tax strategy, regulatory developments and operational priorities into a structured transformation roadmap that addresses material direct and indirect tax requirements.
* Evaluate proposed changes against tax, business, data and technology needs to establish clear scope, outcomes, dependencies and implementation priorities.
* Shape business cases and delivery options for process, data and technology improvements that strengthen tax compliance and operational effectiveness.
* Provide tax transformation insight to process owners and governance forums, enabling informed decisions on investment, sequencing and implementation risk.

**Change Impact & Stakeholder Adoption**

* Assess the impact of tax policy, legislative, process and technology changes on affected teams, controls, data flows and operating procedures.
* Develop and execute change and communication approaches that build stakeholder understanding, readiness and adoption across Group and Country Tax teams.
* Identify adoption barriers and stakeholder concerns early, escalating material issues and coordinating practical mitigation actions with accountable owners.
* Engage Tax, Finance, Technology and business stakeholders to maintain alignment on intended outcomes, responsibilities and implementation requirements.

**Tax Process Optimisation**

* Analyse direct and indirect tax workflows to identify control gaps, duplication, manual intervention and opportunities for standardisation or automation.
* Design improved tax processes and operating practices that enhance accuracy, efficiency, traceability and consistency across relevant jurisdictions.
* Apply process mapping, data analysis and operational requirements analysis to define credible future-state workflows and measurable improvement outcomes.
* Embed continuous improvement mechanisms that use stakeholder feedback, performance information and operational learning to refine tax processes.

**Tax Technology & Data Enablement**

* Define tax business and operational requirements for tax engines, automation tools, data warehouses and reporting platforms in partnership with Technology teams.
* Coordinate tax input into solution design, testing, user acceptance and implementation readiness to confirm that agreed requirements and controls are addressed.
* Support the controlled deployment of tax technologies by coordinating user guidance, adoption support, issue resolution and post-implementation review.
* Monitor solution performance and data outcomes after implementation, directing identified defects, control concerns and enhancement opportunities to accountable owners.

**Transformation Governance, Risk & Controls**

* Establish proportionate governance for tax change initiatives, providing transparent oversight of scope, milestones, dependencies, decisions and delivery risks.
* Integrate tax compliance, internal control and conduct requirements into transformation design and implementation decisions.
* Maintain clear project documentation and performance reporting that enables timely escalation, governance review and accountable decision-making.
* Coordinate the identification, assessment and resolution of tax transformation risks and issues, escalating matters outside the role’s authority to the appropriate owner.

**Legislative & Regulatory Change Readiness**

* Monitor relevant direct and indirect tax developments and assess potential implications for processes, data, controls, systems and reporting obligations.
* Work with tax technical specialists and process owners to convert legislative interpretation into clear operational and technology change requirements.
* Coordinate implementation readiness for regulatory change, ensuring that dependencies, control updates, documentation and stakeholder actions are understood.

Evaluate external tax transformation practices and emerging technologies to identify approaches that may strengthen the Bank’s tax operating environment.

* Responsibility for prioritisation and management of critical path delivery items

title: Senior Principal - Privacy and AI Governance
description:
**Position Summary**
The Privacy and AI Governance Manager will strengthen the assessment, implementation and continuous improvement of PGC’s privacy and AI governance programs. The individual will closely partner with business, Technology, Cybersecurity, Legal, Procurement, HR, and product teams to embed privacy and AI governance requirements throughout the data and AI lifecycles - from ideation and collection through design, development, deployment, monitoring, retention, and decommissioning. The individual will also identify and help operationalize privacy and HIPAA obligations arising from customer contracts and Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) throughout the customer contractual lifecycle.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Privacy Governance**

* Manage the data privacy governance framework, with particular focus on the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and other applicable privacy requirements.
* Identify HIPAA and data privacy obligations arising from external customer contracts and Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), ensure appropriate safeguards are implemented through the contractual lifecycle, including handling of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI). Coordinate implementation and ongoing compliance with applicable safeguards.
* Conduct privacy risk assessments, gap assessments, Data Protection Impact Assessments, and remediation tracking for business processes and applications.
* Maintain governance for privacy notices, consent and withdrawal, data-principal rights, records of processing activities, purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, disposal, data flows, and cross-functional accountability.
* Develop and deliver role-based privacy awareness, communications, and training for employees, leaders, process owners and other relevant groups.
* Act as the single point of contact for data privacy matters, providing practical advisory support that ensures compliance requirements are met.

**AI Governance**

* Operationalize AI governance framework covering entity-level and use-case-level risks and controls across the full AI lifecycle.
* Maintain a standardized AI risk taxonomy, risk and control library, assessment methodology, evidence requirements, maturity criteria, and reporting approach.
* Assess AI control design and operating effectiveness; collaborate with respective control owners to elevate governance maturity and follow through to closure.
* Review AI use cases and provide subject matter expertise on privacy exposures and necessary safeguards.
* Support strengthening policies and procedures on AI governance across variety of use cases (generative AI, large and small language models, agentic AI, enterprise AI, native AI, and third-party AI solutions).
* Align the program, as appropriate, with recognized frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, healthcare AI guidance, and Providence AI principles.
* Monitor regulatory and industry developments and recommend timely updates to policies, controls, training, and governance practices.

**Qualifications and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in law, information technology, cybersecurity. Postgraduate qualification is preferred.
* 8–12 years of experience in privacy, data protection, technology risk, compliance, information governance, AI governance, or related areas, including experience leading cross-functional programs.

who serves as the organization’s subject matter expert in managing and responding to external and internal software license audits. This role is central to ensuring audit readiness, supporting vendor audits, and interpreting complex licensing models and entitlements. The ideal candidate brings deep understanding of the software audit landscape, risk exposure analysis, and vendor compliance enforcement. This position will partner closely with procurement, legal, IT, and finance teams to maintain audit controls and support enterprise compliance with license agreements. The candidate must be willing to work on site 4 days a week in Hyderabad, during US EST time zone.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Audit Response & Management:**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for software and vendor license audits initiated by third-party vendors or auditors.

* Manage audit timelines and ensure audit activities are conducted efficiently and within legal and contractual boundaries.

**Audit Landscape & Risk Profiling:**

* Develop and maintain an audit risk matrix based on vendor contract terms, license models, and past audit history.

**Licensing Compliance Analysis:**

* Analyze software entitlements, deployment data, and actual usage across environments (on-premise, cloud, hybrid).
* Compare usage vs. entitlement to identify under-licensing, over-licensing, or misaligned deployments.
* Provide licensing expertise and interpretations of complex licensing models (SaaS, perpetual, subscription, consumption-based).

**Documentation & Controls:**

* Maintain audit documentation libraries including vendor correspondence, contract terms, deployment evidence, and audit reports.
* Develop and improve audit response templates, checklists, and workflows to ensure consistent and defensible audit responses.
* Support the creation and maintenance of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for audit handling and software license control.

**Stakeholder Engagement & Reporting:**

* Partner with internal stakeholders to explain audit findings, recommend corrective actions, and support remediation.
* Deliver periodic reports and dashboards on audit status, exposure, and trends to executive leadership and compliance committees.
* Provide advisory support during contract renewals or renegotiations to address past audit issues and future compliance planning.

**Audit Preparedness & Education:**

* Lead internal mock audits or dry runs to evaluate readiness for upcoming vendor audits.
* Conduct awareness sessions and training for IT and procurement stakeholders on license audit risks and mitigation strategies.

**Skills & Knowledge**

* Strong understanding of software licensing models (perpetual, SaaS, subscription, user/device-based, cloud usage).
* Familiarity with contract language related to licensing and audit rights.
* Working knowledge of audit processes, risk management, and compliance frameworks.
* High attention to detail in interpreting licensing terms, product use rights (PURs), and deployment metrics.
* Strong project management, coordination, and documentation skills.

**Tools & Systems:**

* Experience with SAM tools (e.g., Flexera, Snow, ServiceNow Software Asset Management, Aspera).
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, data analysis) and collaboration tools (e.g., SharePoint, Teams, PowerPoint).
* Familiarity with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle) and ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow) a plus.

**Cultural Awareness**
Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and manage teams across different time zones.
  
  
**Analytical Thinking**
Ability to interpret and cross-reference large datasets and licensing entitlements.
  
  
**Negotiation Awareness**
Understanding how audit outcomes impact vendor relationships and contract negotiations.
  
  
**Risk Management**
Ability to assess, communicate, and mitigate audit risks effectively.
  
  
**Stakeholder Communication**
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, especially under time-sensitive audit scrutiny.
  
  
**Discretion & Integrity**
Must handle sensitive vendor communications and legal matters with the utmost confidentiality.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**

title: GRC & Data Privacy Analyst
description:
****Role Overview****
We are seeking a detail-oriented GRC & Data Privacy Analyst to join our security team. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining our integrated risk management framework while taking a lead role in implementing and auditing our data privacy program. You will ensure that our operations remain compliant with global regulations (GDPR, PDPA, etc.) while identifying and mitigating risks across the organization.
  
  
****Key Responsibilities****
****Governance & Risk Management****

* Framework Alignment: Maintain and mature the organization’s security framework (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2 and Singapore MAS).
* Risk Assessments: Conduct annual and project-based risk assessments; maintain the Corporate Risk Register and track remediation efforts.
* Policy Management: Draft, review, and update internal security policies and standards to ensure they reflect current business processes.
* Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM): Evaluate the security posture of vendors and partners through assessments and due diligence reviews.

****Data Privacy Implementation****

* Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs/DPIAs): Lead the evaluation of new products or processes to ensure "Privacy by Design" is integrated into the development lifecycle.
* Data Mapping: Maintain a comprehensive record of processing activities (ROPA) and data flow diagrams.
* Privacy Operations: Manage the Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) process and coordinate responses to privacy-related inquiries.
* Compliance Monitoring: Monitor changes in global privacy laws and translate them into actionable technical or procedural requirements for the IT and Product teams.

****Compliance & Auditing****

* Internal Audits: Perform regular control testing to ensure ongoing compliance with internal policies and external regulations.
* External Audit Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors during certification cycles.
* Awareness Training: Develop and deliver training content on security best practices and data handling requirements for all employees.

**Required Qualifications**

* Experience: 8 - 10 years in GRC, Information Security, or IT Audit, with at least 2–4 years specifically focused on Data Privacy.
* Certifications (Preferred): CISA, CRISC, or CISM.
* Technical Skills: Familiarity with GRC tools (Sprinto) and a solid understanding of cloud security (AWS).
* Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of GDPR, PDPA, and industry standards like ISO 27001, SOC 2 and Singapore MAS

****Soft Skills for Success****

* The "Translator" Ability: Can explain complex legal requirements to developers and technical risks to executives.
* Analytical Rigor: A passion for documentation and a "trust but verify" mindset.
* Adaptability: Comfortable navigating the gray areas of emerging privacy legislation.

description:
**About Parexel**
Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insights-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. With 22,000+ employees worldwide, we partner with biopharmaceutical companies and research sites to design and deliver patient-focused clinical trials that broaden access and make research a care option for anyone, anywhere.
  
  
We work with focus, agility, and shared purpose, moving with urgency to address patient needs and accelerate the delivery of new therapies. We embrace bold thinking, adapt quickly to change, and continually raise the bar for the speed and quality of clinical research. We are expanding our team and seeking talented individuals to help drive industry-leading innovations. With Heart.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Proposals and Contracts Specialist, you will support clinical research activities that advance new treatments for patients. This position plays a key role in shaping the proposals and contracts that bring new clinical studies to life, from receipt of the Request for Proposal (RFP) through to client signature. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, follow established SOPs and departmental guidance, and contribute to study operations from proposal preparation through contract finalization.
  
  
Responsibilities include managing the full RFP process, developing strategic proposals and budgets, and creating, negotiating, and finalizing contracts, with opportunities to deepen your expertise and grow your influence in proposal and contract strategy.
  
  
You will join a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment focused on making a meaningful impact through accurate budgets, sound contract strategy, and high-quality client deliverables. With diverse teams and continuous learning opportunities, the Proposals and Contracts Specialist can explore career paths and expand skills across clinical research.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Create, negotiate, and finalize contracts in accordance with departmental SOPs, guidance, and work instructions, drafting Parexel templates in conjunction with relevant departments.
* Manage the RFP process from receipt to delivery, including reviewing RFP documentation and study protocols or synopses, assigning and notifying Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and identifying and mitigating barriers and risks to completion.
* Prepare and modify strategic proposals and budgets in response to RFPs and revisions, using SME feedback and proposal management support, in line with the Decision Rights policy.
* Lead and facilitate client meetings to negotiate costs and terms by the targeted client signature date, negotiating independently or with support depending on contract complexity.
* Develop contract strategies and contract plans for delivery and client signature, with accountable team members.
* Amend project and client budgets in partnership with project and functional teams, using internal tools and reports to ensure all information is included from all groups.
* Ensure proposals, budgets, and contract documents align with the RFP, client specifications and communications, and internal assumptions.
* Obtain third-party quotes as needed and map client bid-grids, with support as needed.
* Deliver quality client deliverables to strict deadlines, including formatted client grids that clearly present the rationale for cost changes.
* Identify contractual issues that require finance, tax, or other internal stakeholder input, and apply lessons learned to similar scenarios in new contracts.
* Keep all documents and files saved in the appropriate locations and data current in the systems used for metrics and KPI purposes, such as Salesforce.
* Attend relevant meetings, build relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and manage time and workload to meet internal and external deadlines, including preparing detailed handoffs before time off.

**Candidate Profile**
**You'll Thrive In This Role If You Bring**

* Strong understanding of the operational aspects of clinical study conduct in different regions of the world, which may be demonstrated through previous work experience in the industry
* Excellent analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to perform several tasks simultaneously
* A consistent commitment to high-quality work and outstanding attention to detail
* Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to make effective, appropriate decisions when necessary
* Sound judgment about when to bring in support or escalate difficult situations and interactions
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, highly developed interpersonal skills, and a strong team orientation
* Confidence interacting with all levels of staff and the ability to lead internal and client meetings
* The ability to meet deadlines independently while managing multiple, varied tasks with enthusiasm and prioritizing workload
* Willingness to work in a matrix environment and to value the importance of teamwork
* A sense of urgency and a positive attitude in everything you do

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree in Life Science, Business, Languages, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
* At least three years of previous experience in project support, finance, contracting, or proposals in a CRO or similar environment
* Standard knowledge of proposal and contract management principles, contractual terms, pricing structures, and pricing tools and data systems (e.g., Salesforce)
* Higher-level knowledge of relevant software, including Windows, Word, Excel, Outlook, and databases
* Fluent in written and oral English
* Ability to work from home
* Ability to work irregular and/or extended hours as needed to meet the client's proposal deadline

title: General Manager - Corporate EXIM
description:
**About the Company:**

**Larsen & Toubro Ltd, commonly known as L&T,**
is an Indian multinational conglomerate company, with business interests in engineering, construction, manufacturing, technology, information technology and financial services, headquartered in Mumbai. The company is counted among world's top five construction companies.

The L&T Group comprises of 93 subsidiaries, 5 associate companies, 27 joint ventures and 35 jointly held operations, operating across basic and heavy engineering, construction, realty, manufacturing of capital goods, information technology, and financial services.

**This role is based out of Powai, Mumbai.**

**Job Responsibilities:**

**1. DGFT Licensing & Advance Authorization Management**

* Lead end-to-end management of Advance Authorization, EPCG, IEC, RCMC, RoDTEP and other DGFT approvals.
* Handle and close high-volume and high-value Advance Authorizations, including application, amendment, invalidation, export obligation tracking, redemption and EODC.
* Ensure timely closure of legacy and current AA cases with accurate documentation, reconciliation and DGFT submissions.
* Monitor license validity, export obligation, duty saved value, import/export utilization and pending closures through periodic dashboards.
* Manage deficiency letters, DGFT queries, show-cause notices, representations and closure-related escalations.

**2. FTP & DGFT Compliance**

* Act as the subject matter expert for Foreign Trade Policy, Handbook of Procedures, DGFT Notifications, Public Notices and Trade Notices.
* Track policy changes and assess impact on imports, exports, licenses, benefits and compliance obligations.
* Develop SOPs, checklists and internal controls for DGFT transactions.
* Ensure compliance for IEC, RCMC, Status Holder, license conditions, export obligations and statutory records.
* Support internal, statutory and regulatory audits relating to DGFT and FTP matters.

**3. DGFT Imports Importability & Classification**

* Review importability of goods under ITC(HS), DGFT policy conditions, restricted/prohibited category requirements and license applicability before import.
* Provide guidance on HS classification alignment for DGFT license applications, Advance Authorization inputs, EPCG imports and restricted item import cases.
* Coordinate with Customs/EXIM operations teams to ensure DGFT licenses, import policy conditions and Customs declarations are aligned.
* Support resolution of import-related classification or policy-condition issues impacting DGFT license utilization or closure.

**4. SCOMET & Export Control Compliance**

* Lead SCOMET compliance monitoring for exports of goods, technology, software, spares, drawings, technical documents and services, wherever applicable.
* Ensure proper screening, classification review, license requirement assessment and adherence to DGFT export-control conditions.
* Maintain SCOMET records, license trackers, end-use/end-user documentation and post-export compliance evidence.
* Conduct SCOMET awareness sessions for Business, Engineering, SCM, Projects, Logistics and EXIM teams.
* Escalate potential export-control risks and ensure no restricted export is undertaken without required approval.

**5. Export Incentives & Benefits**

* Oversee export benefit schemes such as RoDTEP, legacy MEIS/SEIS/FPS, deemed export benefits and other applicable incentives.
* Ensure accurate claim filing, reconciliation, realization tracking and audit-ready documentation.
* Coordinate with Finance and Banking teams for incentive accounting, export proceeds linkage and benefit utilization.

**6. Stakeholder Management & Governance**

* Interface with DGFT Regional Authorities, DGFT HQ, EPCs, Customs teams, consultants and statutory agencies.
* Work closely with Business, SCM, Finance, Projects, Engineering and Logistics teams.
* Lead, guide and review the DGFT compliance team on complex licensing, closure, SCOMET and policy matters.
* Maintain MIS and management dashboards for license status, EODC ageing, SCOMET cases, incentives and audit issues.
* Handle DGFT policy relaxation matters, including preparation and submission of applications/representations before the Policy Relaxation Committee (PRC), wherever required.
* Ensure adequate exposure and capability to manage interactions, representations and follow-ups with DGFT, PRC, EPCG Committee and Norms Committee for approvals, clarifications, regularization and closure of complex cases.

**Experience**

* 23+ years of experience in DGFT licensing, FTP compliance, EXIM and trade regulatory matters.
* Strong experience in managing Advance Authorization and EPCG in high-value, high-volume environments.
* Adequate exposure to handle DGFT, PRC, EPCG Committee and Norms Committee level interactions/ representations.
* Prior exposure to Engineering / EPC / Infrastructure / Manufacturing sectors preferred.
* Proven ability to handle DGFT authorities, deficiency letters, representations, audits and closure of complex licenses.
* Working knowledge of Customs matters such as importability, HS classification and DGFT linked import policy requirements.

**Technical Competencies**

* Expert knowledge of FTP, HBP, DGFT portal, AA, EPCG, IEC, RCMC, RoDTEP and SCOMET.
* Strong hands-on experience in Advance Authorization closure, EODC, amendments, invalidation and redemption.
* Knowledge of ITC(HS), import policy conditions and classification relevance for DGFT imports.
* Adequate understanding of Customs processes to ensure proper alignment of DGFT license requirements with import documentation, classification and clearance-related controls.
* Strong understanding of SCOMET classification, licensing and export-control compliance.
* Proficiency in MS Excel, PowerPoint, ERP systems, MIS dashboards and digital document repositories.

**About Roofsol Energy**

Roofsol Energy Pvt. Ltd. is a leading solar EPC and renewable energy company engaged in developing and executing solar power projects across India. The company operates across rooftop solar, ground-mounted solar, and Open Access projects, with a focus on delivering comprehensive solar energy solutions to commercial, industrial, and institutional clients.

**Position Overview**

Roofsol Energy is looking for an experienced and well-connected
**Head – Government Liaisoning**
to lead and manage government approvals, statutory clearances, regulatory coordination, and liaisoning activities for solar projects across India.

The incumbent will be responsible for developing and maintaining strong working relationships with government authorities, DISCOMs, electricity departments, State Nodal Agencies, transmission utilities, and other relevant regulatory bodies to facilitate timely approvals and smooth project execution.

The role requires extensive experience in the Indian power and renewable energy sector, a strong understanding of state-wise regulatory frameworks, and the ability to lead a pan-India liaisoning team.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Government Approvals & Statutory Clearances**

·      Lead the end-to-end process of obtaining statutory approvals, permits, licenses, and clearances required for rooftop, ground-mounted, and Open Access solar projects.

·      Coordinate with relevant Central and State Government departments, regulatory authorities, and local bodies for project-related approvals.

·      Ensure timely processing of applications, documentation, and compliance requirements for project commissioning.

·      Monitor approval timelines and proactively resolve bottlenecks affecting project execution.

·      Manage a team of talented executives and vendors across the country on a day-to-day basis.

**2. DISCOM & Power Utility Coordination**

·      Develop and maintain strong working relationships with State DISCOMs, electricity boards, transmission utilities, and other power sector authorities.

·      Manage approvals related to grid connectivity, net metering, gross metering, synchronization, and commissioning of rooftop solar projects.

·      Coordinate approvals related to evacuation infrastructure, grid connectivity, and power transmission for ground-mounted and Open Access projects.

·      Facilitate approvals for electrical inspections, CEIG clearances, grid synchronization, and other applicable technical and statutory requirements.

title: Principal Associate - Banking & Finance - Transactions
description:
**Position:**
Principal Associate

**Practice Area:**
Banking & Finance – Transactions

**Experience:**
7–10 Years PQE (preferred)

**Organisation:**
India Law LLP

About the Role

India Law LLP is looking to hire an experienced and result-oriented Principal Associate for its Banking & Finance – Transactions practice.

The ideal candidate should have substantial experience in handling banking and finance transactions, advising lenders and borrowers, negotiating and reviewing finance and security documentation, and managing transactions from inception to closure.

The candidate should possess strong transactional experience, excellent drafting and negotiation skills, commercial understanding, and the ability to independently manage transactions and lead teams.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

* Handle and independently manage banking and finance transactions, including domestic and cross-border financing arrangements.
* Advise banks, financial institutions, NBFCs, corporates, and other stakeholders on various financing structures and transactions.
* Draft, review, negotiate, and finalise financing and security documents, including:Facility Agreements and Loan Agreements.
* Term Loan and Working Capital Facility Documents.
* Hypothecation Agreements.
* Mortgage and Security Documents.
* Guarantee Agreements.
* Deed of Pledge and Assignment Agreements.
* Escrow Agreements and other ancillary transaction documents.
* Conduct legal due diligence and identify legal risks associated with financing transactions.
* Advise on creation, perfection, registration, and enforcement of security interests.
* Coordinate and manage transaction closings, including satisfaction of conditions precedent and conditions subsequent.
* Liaise with clients, banks, financial institutions, lenders, borrowers, and other stakeholders.
* Provide legal opinions and advisory support on banking and finance-related matters.
* Ensure compliance with applicable banking laws, RBI regulations, FEMA provisions, and other relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.
* Independently manage transactions, supervise team members, and ensure timely delivery of assignments.
* Participate in client meetings, negotiations, and transaction structuring discussions.

Required Qualifications & Experience

* LL.B. degree from a recognised university.
* 7–10 years of Post Qualification Experience (PQE) in Banking & Finance transactions.
* Strong hands-on experience in banking and finance documentation and transactional advisory.
* Experience in advising banks, NBFCs, financial institutions, lenders, and borrowers.
* Good understanding of secured and unsecured lending transactions.
* Experience in drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and finalising financing and security documentation.
* Exposure to due diligence, transaction structuring, and transaction closures.
* Sound knowledge of applicable banking laws, RBI regulations, FEMA, and other relevant regulatory frameworks.

Required Skills & Competencies

* Excellent legal drafting, documentation, and negotiation skills.
* Strong commercial and transactional understanding.
* Ability to independently handle and close complex transactions.
* Excellent analytical, research, and problem-solving abilities.
* Strong client management and communication skills.
* Ability to lead, mentor, and supervise junior team members.
* Ability to manage multiple transactions and work within strict timelines.
* A proactive, detail-oriented, and solution-driven approach.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for a commercially oriented legal professional with substantial transactional experience in Banking & Finance, who can independently manage transactions, take ownership of client assignments, negotiate complex documentation, and contribute to the growth of the Banking & Finance practice at India Law LLP.

**Candidates with strong experience in end-to-end banking and finance transactions, lender-side and borrower-side advisory, and independent transaction management will be preferred.**

**Interested candidates can email their CV at hrd@indialaw.in**

title: Assistant Manager - Direct & Indirect Tax
description:
*Business Introduction*
GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.
  
  
Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.
  
  
Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.
  
  
Position Chartered Accountant – Direct Tax & Indirect Tax
  
  
**Experience**
2–3+ years of relevant post-qualification experience
  
  
***Qualification***

* Chartered Accountant (CA) – Qualified with Strong academic and professional understanding of Direct and Indirect Taxation.
* Prior experience in a tax consultancy, CA firm, corporate tax department, or similar environment will be preferred

**Job Overview**
We are looking for a Chartered Accountant with 2–3+ years of relevant experience in Direct Tax and Indirect Tax. The candidate will be responsible for managing tax compliances, tax assessments, litigation, advisory and related tax matters.
  
  
The role will have a strong focus on Indirect Taxation, particularly GST, while also handling Direct Tax matters. The candidate should have hands-on experience in tax compliance and litigation and possess the ability to independently handle routine tax matters.
  
  
***Key Responsibilities***

* Indirect Tax :
* Review of Input & Output Register monthly for all the three company
* Review GST transactions and advise business teams on the taxability and GST implications of transactions.
* Handle GST-related notices, queries, assessments and departmental correspondence.
* Support IDT Manager in replying to GST notices and coordinate with tax authorities.
* Assist Tax Manager in GST audits, departmental audits, assessments and investigations.
* Assist in GST litigation and appeals at various levels.
* Monitor changes in GST laws, notifications, circulars, orders and case laws and assess their impact on the business.
* Review tax positions relating to ITC, RCM, place of supply, valuation, classification, exemptions and GST rates.
* Assist in GST refund applications and related follow-up.
* Coordinate with internal teams, consultants and external tax advisors on data compilation and relevant record for appeals.
* Support implementation of process improvements and automation in GST compliance and reporting.
* Direct Tax
* Assist in Data Compilation for Tax Assessment, Appeals and Court cases
* Preparation/review of Agreements/Contract for TDS & GST Applicability
* Review of Transfer Pricing Audit Report/Study Report
* Review of third Party benchmark studies
* Assist in preparation of responses to Income Tax notices/Tax default Notice.
* Assist in Income Tax assessments, appeals and litigation.
* Coordinate with tax consultants and authorities for Direct Tax matters.
* Monitor changes in Income Tax law, circulars, notifications and judicial developments.
* Tax Litigation & Assessments
* Assist Tax Head in handling tax notices, assessments and departmental proceedings.
* Assist in preparation of factual and legal submissions in consultation with senior management/tax advisors.
* Coordinate with consultants and legal professionals for tax litigation.
* Maintain records of notices, submissions, orders and appeal proceedings.
* Track litigation matters and ensure timely compliance with procedural requirements.
* Research relevant provisions, circulars, notifications and judicial precedents.
* Ensure Contingent Liability file and update regularly for the Internal Stake holder
* Maintain Tax related entry on timely manner for Refunds, Demand Paid any internal adjustment etc.
* Tax Advisory & Business Support
* Provide tax inputs to finance and business teams on day-to-day transactions.
* Review proposed business transactions from a Direct Tax and Indirect Tax perspective.
* Identify tax risks and suggest appropriate compliance measures.
* Assist in tax planning and implementation within the applicable legal framework.
* Prepare tax-related MIS, reports and management updates.
* Ensure timely escalation of significant tax risks and potential exposures.

***Key Skills & Competencies***
Mandatory
  
  

* Strong practical knowledge of GST and Indirect Taxation
* Good working knowledge of Income Tax and TDS
* Hands-on experience in tax compliance
* Practical exposure to tax notices, assessments and litigation
* Ability to independently handle routine tax matters
* Strong knowledge of GST law, rules, notifications, circulars and relevant case laws
* Good analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and drafting skills
* Ability to coordinate with internal teams, consultants and tax authorities
* Good working knowledge of MS Excel and other relevant tax/compliance systems

**Preferred**

* Experience in handling complex GST issues such as RCM, place of supply, valuation, classification and input tax credit
* Exposure to tax advisory and transaction review
* Experience working in a corporate tax environment or reputed CA/tax firm

***Candidate Profile***
The ideal candidate should be:
  
  

* A qualified Chartered Accountant
* Having 2–3+ years of post-qualification experience
* Strong in Direct Tax & Indirect Tax/GST, with adequate knowledge of Direct Tax
* Experienced in tax compliances as well as litigation/assessments
* Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of tax matters
* Detail-oriented with strong analytical and drafting capabilities
* Proactive in identifying tax risks and keeping up with changes in tax laws
* Capable of working with business, finance, legal and external tax consultants

***Key Focus of the Role***

* Indirect Tax / GST 50%
* Direct Tax 50%

**Preferred Experience**
Candidates having practical experience in Direct Tax Compliance, Transfer Pricing Regulations, DT Litigations, TP Litigations, TDS Litigations, GST compliance, GST assessments, GST notices, GST litigation, ITC reconciliation and GST advisory will be preferred.
  
  
**Skills**
Business Acumen, Critical Thinking, Digital Fluency, Enterprise Thinking, Influencing Without Authority, Problem Solving, Tax Management
  
  
**Why GSK?**
**Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.**
GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.
  
  
People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.
  
  
**Inclusion at GSK:**
As an employer committed to Inclusion, we encourage you to reach out if you need any adjustments during the recruitment process.
  
  
Please contact our Recruitment Team at IN.recruitment-adjustments@gsk.com to discuss your needs.
  
  
**Important notice to Employment businesses/ Agencies**
GSK does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact GSK's commercial and general procurement/human resources department to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to GSK. The obtaining of prior written authorization is a condition precedent to any agreement (verbal or written) between the employment business/ agency and GSK. In the absence of such written authorization being obtained any actions undertaken by the employment business/agency shall be deemed to have been performed without the consent or contractual agreement of GSK. GSK shall therefore not be liable for any fees arising from such actions or any fees arising from any referrals by employment businesses/agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site.

Please be advised that such advertisements and emails are not connected with the GlaxoSmithKline group in any way.
  
  
**GlaxoSmithKline does not charge any fee whatsoever for recruitment process. Please do not make payments to any individuals / entities in connection with recruitment with any GlaxoSmithKline (or GSK) group company at any worldwide location. Even if they claim that the money is refundable.**

title: Associate Advocate
description:
Job Title: Associate Advocate – Corporate Legal & Litigation

Company: Konark Group

Department: Legal & Compliance

Employment Type: Full-Time

Experience: 5-8 Years

Location: Corporate Office, Maharashtra

Qualification: LL.B. (Enrolled with the Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa)

Job Overview

Konark Group is looking for a dedicated, proactive and detail-oriented Associate Advocate to join its in-house legal team.

The candidate will be responsible for handling the company’s day-to-day legal matters, litigation coordination, drafting and vetting of legal documents, government contracts, tender-related legal issues and regulatory compliance.

The role involves working closely with the management, tendering, finance, HR, accounts and project execution teams to protect the company’s legal and commercial interests.

The ideal candidate should have practical experience in civil and commercial litigation, contract drafting, government tenders and dealing with legal matters involving Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils and other government authorities.

Key Responsibilities

1. Litigation & Court Matters

* Handle and coordinate ongoing civil, criminal, commercial and contractual litigation.
* Draft legal notices, replies, affidavits, applications, written statements and other pleadings.
* Coordinate with external advocates, senior counsels and law firms.
* Track court cases, hearing dates, orders, deadlines and compliance requirements.
* Maintain a centralised litigation register and case-wise documentation.
* Prepare case briefs, chronologies and supporting documents for senior advocates.
* Attend court proceedings and represent the company wherever legally authorised.

2. Corporate & Commercial Legal Matters

* Draft, review and vet commercial agreements, service agreements, work orders, MoUs and NDAs.
* Review contractual obligations, indemnity clauses, penalties, liquidated damages and termination provisions.
* Advise internal departments on contractual risks and legal implications.
* Assist in resolving commercial disputes with clients, vendors, contractors and subcontractors.
* Ensure appropriate legal documentation for the company’s business transactions.

3. Government Tender & Contract Legal Support

* Review tender documents from a legal and contractual perspective.
* Examine eligibility conditions, disqualification clauses, blacklisting provisions and termination clauses.
* Assist in preparing legal representations, objections, pre-bid queries and tender-related replies.
* Review LOAs, agreements, performance guarantees and contractual commitments.
* Analyse show-cause notices, warning letters, penalty orders and proposed termination notices.
* Assist in challenging arbitrary or discriminatory tender conditions through appropriate legal remedies.
* Coordinate with tender and project teams on contractual disputes with government authorities.

4. Government & Regulatory Correspondence

* Draft replies to notices and communications received from government departments.
* Prepare legal representations to Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, Urban Development Departments and other authorities.
* Coordinate with regulatory authorities and government departments on legal issues.
* Monitor changes in applicable laws, government resolutions, circulars and statutory requirements.
* Maintain records of legal notices, government communications and submissions.

5. Labour Law & Employment Matters

* Assist HR in handling employee disputes, disciplinary proceedings and termination matters.
* Draft employment agreements, warning letters, show-cause notices and settlement documents.
* Support the company in matters involving labour laws, PF, ESIC, wages and statutory employment compliance.
* Coordinate with labour consultants and external advocates for employment-related disputes.

6. Legal Research & Risk Management

* Conduct legal research on applicable laws, judgments, government resolutions and regulatory notifications.
* Research matters involving BNS, BNSS, CPC, Contract Act, Arbitration Act and applicable procurement rules.
* Prepare legal opinions and risk assessment notes for management.
* Identify potential legal exposure in projects, contracts and business transactions.
* Maintain a legal database of important judgments and precedents relevant to the company’s business.

7. Internal Legal Coordination

* Work closely with Tendering, HR, Finance, Accounts, Operations and Project Management teams.
* Obtain factual inputs and supporting documents before preparing legal responses.
* Maintain confidentiality of sensitive company information and litigation strategy.
* Ensure all legal deadlines and statutory timelines are complied with.
* Provide periodic updates to management regarding critical legal matters.

Educational Qualifications & Experience

* LL.B. degree from a recognised university.
* Must be enrolled with the Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa.
* 2–5 years of experience in litigation, corporate legal work or infrastructure-related legal matters.
* Practical experience in drafting legal notices, pleadings, affidavits and commercial agreements.
* Familiarity with Indian courts, tribunals and government departments.
* Good command of English, Hindi and Marathi.

Preferred Experience

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in:

* Infrastructure and construction companies.
* Solid Waste Management contracts.
* Water supply and municipal infrastructure projects.
* Government tender disputes and procurement matters.
* Civil and commercial litigation.
* Arbitration and contractual disputes.
* Labour and employment-related litigation.

* Timely preparation and filing of legal documents.

title: Senior Specialist Employee Relations
description:
**Role Overview**
The ER Specialist will be responsible for managing Employee Relations (ER), Industrial Relations (IR), contract labor administration, statutory compliance, and workforce engagement. The role requires strong people management skills, hands-on experience with labor laws, government liaison, and data-driven HR reporting.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Employee & Industrial Relations**

* Manage Employee Relations (ER) and Industrial Relations (IR) activities across the organization.
* Handle employee grievances, disciplinary actions, domestic inquiries, and conflict resolution.
* Maintain healthy industrial relations with workmen, unions (if applicable), and internal stakeholders.
* Support management in negotiations, settlements, and dispute resolution.

**Contract Labor Management**

* End-to-end management of contract labor including onboarding, attendance, deployment, and exit.
* Ensure compliance with Contract Labor (Regulation & Abolition) Act and other applicable labor laws.
* Coordinate with contractors for manpower planning and performance monitoring.

**Payroll & Vendor Coordination**

* Supervise and validate contract payroll processing in coordination with vendors.
* Ensure accuracy of wages, statutory deductions, and timely disbursement.
* Audit contractor bills and payroll records for compliance and correctness.

**Statutory & Legal Compliance**

* Ensure 100% compliance with applicable labor laws (Factories Act, Shops & Establishments Act, PF, ESI, Minimum Wages, Bonus, Gratuity, etc.).
* Prepare and file statutory returns, registers, and records within timelines.
* Handle inspections, audits, and queries from labor authorities.
* Coordinate with legal advisors on labor-related cases and compliance matters.

* Manage preparation, renewal, and maintenance of statutory licenses and registrations.
* Handle submission of statutory returns and responses to notices.

**Employee Engagement & People Management**

* Plan and execute employee engagement activities to improve morale and workplace culture.
* Support initiatives related to employee communication, welfare, and retention.
* Act as a bridge between management and employees to foster trust and transparency.

* Prepare MIS reports and presentations for management review.
